title: VPC Warden Terraform module: security group/NACL/PrivateDNS/Egress guardrails
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Create a reusable Terraform module (vpc-warden) that codifies VPC security guardrails for Private deployments. The module must provide declarative security groups, NACL templates, private Route53 DNS zones and records, and opinionated egress policies (proxying, explicit allowlists, optional NAT alternatives). It should include conversion helpers for existing stacks, idempotent upgrade paths, automated health checks (DNS resolution, egress probe, flow logs sink) and an optional drift-detection hook that emits alerts to our Console. Aim for composability so Dedicated and Hosted migration recipes can consume the module with minimal overrides.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module published to private registry with semver tags
Module exposes variables for security group rules, NACL templates, private DNS zone names, and egress policy mode (proxy|nat|deny-with-allowlist)

Automated smoke health-check Terraform null_resource runs that validate: private DNS resolution for internal service records, outbound egress to allowed IPs via configured path, and that Flow Logs are forwarding to the central logging account
Upgrade path documented for clusters using legacy-sg/legacy-nacl with migration script and zero-downtime rule application
CI pipeline runs 'terraform plan' with the module and rejects unsafe changes (e.g., opening 0.0.0.0/0 for SSH in prod) via policy checks
Playbook for on-call with straightforward rollback steps and an automated rollback flag in the module input
implementation_steps: Design module API: inputs, outputs, and recommended variable defaults; review with Security & Infra
Implement core resources: aws_security_group, aws_network_acl, aws_route53_zone + aws_route53_record, VPC endpoints for logging and S3
Add egress_policy submodule supporting 'proxy', 'nat', 'deny-with-allowlist' modes with examples
Implement health checks as optional null_resource triggers that run an internal test harness via AWS Systems Manager Run Command
Integrate Flow Logs + centralized s3/cloudwatch sink and validate permissions via IAM roles
Add Terraform tests using kitchen-terraform and unit tests for policy generation logic
Create migration script (terraform import helpers + state move examples) and a dry-run doc
Add pre-merge policy checks (tflint + custom rules) and Sentinel/policy-as-code gates in CI
Publish to private registry and create example consumers under infra-examples repo
rollout_plan: Start with a canary in staging VPC: deploy module in 'audit' mode (no deny rules enforced) and run health-checks for 72 hours. Next, pick one low-traffic customer-facing VPC in Dedicated as a pilot with egress set to 'proxy' and apply NAT fallback. If canary passes, roll out to a small batch of VPCs using Terraform workspaces and a staged approval job. Each batch must run automated preflight plan checks and health-checks before approval. Full prod enablement requires Security sign-off and a 48-hour monitoring window.
testing_plan: Unit tests for rule generation (go + testify) covering tag-based rule composition
Integration tests in a sandbox VPC validating Route53 private record creation and resolution
End-to-end egress smoke test: ensure HTTP(S) egress travels through configured proxy and that direct egress is blocked when deny-with-allowlist is enabled
Chaos test: simulate instance replacement to validate no rule staleness or transient outage
Regression tests for migration script to confirm that imported resources reconcile to module-managed state
notes: Prefer immutability for critical outputs: don't change security_group IDs between major versions; expose new rules as additional resources to avoid replace operations
We should provide both 'managed' and 'bring-your-own' modes for DNS: managed creates private zone and records, BYO attaches records via terraform_remote_state
Consider an opt-in 'egress-profile' dataset that maps typical workloads to recommendations (latency-sensitive -> proxy with keepalive; batch -> nat)
Discussed a drift detection PoC: background AWS Config rule that compares live SG/NACL to Terraform plan; if mismatch emit Console alert. Might be scoped to v1.1
infra_changes: New IAM role for Flow Logs writing to central account
Optional SSM document for health-check runner
Route53 private zones will be created in customer-owned accounts when managed=true
followup_tasks: Add Grafana dashboards for module-specific metrics (egress hits, policy denies, DNS failures)
Create migration runbook and a one-click rollback Terraform variable
Coordinate with Platform team to surface module status in Redwood Console
